meta.title: The 7 secrets of the most-watched names online
meta.description: An interactive guide to clipping: why your own page has a ceiling, and how the most-watched artists, streamers and brands get around it.

opening.headline: The most-watched names online aren’t posting more.
opening.sub: They are being posted by everyone else. Seven secrets on how that works, and how to make it work for you. About eight minutes.
opening.counterLabel: views from the four campaigns on this wall

secrets.title: Your own page has a ceiling
secrets.lead: Every post you make is tested on a small circle first. If that circle does not react fast enough, the post stops there.

test.label: Try it
test.testing: Shown to a small test circle
test.pushed: Pushed out. The platform shows it to more people.
test.stopped: Stopped. Not enough reaction in the first hour.

slider.label: Your followers
slider.gap: The gap is the ceiling. More followers move it up, but never close it.

body: Followers raise the ceiling, but they never remove it. The people you are trying to reach are mostly not following you yet, and the platform has no reason to show them a page they have never seen.

secrets.title: You see them everywhere, but rarely on their own page
secrets.lead: Scroll a feed and the same song, show or product comes back again and again. Almost none of those posts come from the artist or the brand.

feed.label: Tap a clip to see who posted it
feed.note: Five clips from one campaign. Page types shown as examples.

pages.label: One post or many pages
pages.total: total views if each page gets about {per}

same.label: Same moment, six pages
same.caption: The same moment, posted six times by six different pages, each to its own audience.

body: Each page brings its own audience. When enough pages post the same moment in the same week, the platform starts treating it as something people want, and pushes it to everyone else.

secrets.title: Ads rent attention at the highest price
secrets.lead: An ad is paid for every time it is shown, and the views stop the day the budget does.

calc.label: Your budget
calc.chartNote: Views per month at the middle of each range. Clips stay up after the budget ends; ads do not.

body: Clipping costs a fraction per view because you pay for counted views on real posts, and those posts keep collecting views long after the campaign is paid for.

secrets.title: Artists, streamers and brands are all doing it
secrets.lead: The biggest names online run this play on purpose. Once you know it, you see it everywhere.

yacht.live: A stream on a yacht. A handful of people watching.
yacht.clipsTitle: What the clips made it look like
yacht.clips: The same stream cut into dozens of moments, posted by dozens of pages. Everyone saw it.
yacht.note: Drawn to show the idea. Not real footage.

cards.label: paid out to 303 clippers in one campaign
views from clips of one creator

body: None of them rely on their own page alone. They make the moment, then let hundreds of other pages carry it.

secrets.title: Pay for results, not posts
secrets.lead: Pay per 1,000 counted views, with a minimum before a clip earns and a cap so one clip cannot take the budget.

sim.below: Below the minimum: nothing paid yet
sim.presetCaption: A Kojo Blak clip from the campaign: 1.9M views, capped at $300.

body: Every view past the cap is free. The best clip in a campaign often brings most of its views at no extra cost.

secrets.title: The fastest way to burn your first $1,000
secrets.lead: Bought views look like results until you check them. Every botted clip you approve takes money out of the budget.

game.label: Spot the bot
game.score: You caught {right} of {total}. The bots you let through would have cost you ${cost}.
game.perfect: You caught all {total}. That is the job, on every clip, every day.

cards.why: Views climb and level off, engagement and watch time look human, the audience matches the market.
A vertical jump in one hour, almost no likes or comments, a new account, and countries nowhere near the target.
Slow, steady growth and strong engagement. Small numbers are not a warning sign.
A perfectly straight line is not how people watch. Watch time of 6% means nobody stayed.
A fast start that slows down is how a clip that lands behaves.
Views arrive in identical blocks, as if bought in packs.

warning.title: Before you use an open marketplace
warning.text: Open clipping marketplaces such as Content Rewards let anyone submit. That is how most first campaigns lose money: botted clips get approved because nobody checked them.
warning.rule: The admin rule: nobody gets paid until a person has opened the clip, checked the views, the engagement, the account and the countries, and approved it.

secrets.title: Fit beats volume
secrets.lead: A million views from the wrong people is worth less than a hundred thousand from the right ones. Pick the pages that already serve your audience.

Music: Fan pages of artists in the same genre
Brands: Lifestyle pages that match the buyer
Meme pages with the right audience
Creators: Meme pages that share the humour
